History and Physical (H&P – Detailed)

Consult Summary:
32-year-old male with 4-day history of sore throat, nasal congestion, and new dry cough; symptoms consistent with a viral upper respiratory tract infection.  

History:
• Onset/Timeline
  – Day 0 (4 days ago): Sudden sore throat, painful swallowing, clear rhinorrhea, subjective fever.  
  – Day 2: Throat pain improving; persistent nasal congestion.  
  – Day 3: Intermittent night sweats and myalgias begin.  
  – Day 4 (yesterday): New constant dry cough; continues today.  
• Current symptoms
  – Dry, non-productive cough (constant).  
  – Nasal congestion/stuffy nose; rhinorrhea now clearing.  
  – Fatigue, generalized muscle aches.  
  – Intermittent generalized headaches.  
  – Night sweats.  
  – Mild exertional dyspnea; no dyspnea at rest, no chest pain.  
  – Reduced appetite, increased fluid intake.  
• Exacerbating/Relieving factors
  – Acetaminophen and ibuprofen reduce fever and malaise.  
• Associated review of systems
  – ENT: No ear pain/discharge; no visual changes, photophobia, oral lesions.  
  – GI/GU: No nausea, vomiting, diarrhea; bowels and urination normal.  
  – Derm: No rash.  
  – MSK: New generalized myalgias; no joint swelling.  

Past Medical History:
• No chronic medical conditions reported.

Medications:
• Acetaminophen – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Ibuprofen – dose/route/frequency not documented.

Allergies:
• No known drug allergies.

Social History:
• Lives alone; works as an accountant.  
• Smoking: Occasional cigars at company functions.  
• Alcohol: Occasional, social.  
• No recreational drug use mentioned.  
• Reports increased work-related stress during year-end period but denies mood issues.

Family History:
• Maternal grandmother: Type 2 diabetes mellitus.  
• Great-grandfather: Eczema.  
• No other significant familial illnesses disclosed.

Physical Examination:
• No vital signs or physical findings documented in transcript.

Investigations:
• None performed or recorded during consult.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Viral upper respiratory tract infection / probable early influenza
  • Plan
    – Supportive care: rest, maintain hydration.  
    – Continue acetaminophen and ibuprofen as needed for fever, pain.  
    – Off-work note for 1–2 days recommended.  
    – Return precautions: seek care sooner for high fever, worsening shortness of breath, chest pain, or lack of improvement.  
    – Routine follow-up next week if symptoms persist or worsen.

General Plan items
  • Educated on viral illness course (typically 7–10 days).  
  • Offered discussion of stress/mood support if needed in future.

Quality checks:

Missing/expected elements
• Vital signs, physical examination, and objective findings absent.  
• Medication dosages, route, and exact frequency not documented.  
• Vaccination status (e.g., influenza, COVID-19) not addressed.

Internal conflicts
• None noted.

Transcript quality
• Clear, minor conversational filler; no inaudible sections impacting data extraction.
